excerpt: Compare buying and renting on Al Reem Island over the same period, including transaction costs, owner expenses, flexibility and capital tied up.
introduction:
Buying on Al Reem Island can provide control over a home and an asset to sell later, while renting can preserve flexibility and avoid a buyer's upfront transaction costs. The cheaper choice depends on the exact apartment, intended stay, financing, future sale value and what your capital could otherwise earn.

Compare similar homes over the same period. The figures below provide a worked comparison of buying and renting over the same period.
takeaways: Include acquisition, ownership and sale costs as well as the uncertain future sale price.
Compare rent, deposits, notice and moving costs for a similar apartment over the same period.
Account for the timing and opportunity cost of capital, and check current Abu Dhabi tenancy rules.

sections.heading: What belongs in the comparison?
sections.body:
For a purchase, include the price, registration and brokerage, finance charges if relevant, annual service charges, insurance and maintenance. At the end of the period, include the assumed sale price, selling costs and remaining loan. The result is sensitive to the price at which the home can actually be sold.

For a rental, include rent, non-refundable lease charges, utilities, moving and any permitted renewal changes. Keep refundable deposits as a cash requirement and record any later deduction separately. Compare homes with similar size, condition, parking and facilities.

The [Al Reem and Al Raha family guide](/journal/al-reem-island-vs-al-raha-beach-for-family-living) helps assess the daily routine and building. The actual unit and agreement determine the cost.

sections.heading: A simplified five-year example
sections.body:
Imagine a cash purchase for AED 1,200,000, with AED 60,000 acquisition costs, AED 15,000 annual owner costs for five years and AED 30,000 selling costs. If the property sells for the same AED 1,200,000, the simplified ownership cost is AED 165,000.

Imagine a comparable rental at AED 85,000 a year for five years, totalling AED 425,000. These example inputs show how each purchase and rental cost fits into the comparison. The chart excludes tenant fees, moving, financing, tax and the return that might have been earned on capital. The flat rent is an illustration, not a prediction of future rent or a statement of the rules.

If the eventual sale price is AED 200,000 lower, the simplified ownership cost becomes AED 365,000 under the other assumptions. A real comparison must account for all cash-flow dates and the uncertainty of the sale.

sections.heading: Account for capital and financing
sections.body:
The buyer in the example commits AED 1,260,000 at the start, while the renter may keep capital and pay rent over time. Model the return that could reasonably be earned on available funds and the timing of payments on both sides. An assumed return is not guaranteed.

With a mortgage, use the actual down payment, bank fees, interest, principal payments and remaining balance at sale. A variable rate, refinance or early settlement can change the result. Do not count principal repayment as a cost without also accounting for the reduced loan balance.

For a material decision, a discounted cash-flow model and qualified financial advice can help compare the different timing of cash flows.

sections.heading: Check current tenancy rules
sections.body:
ADREC announced a [temporary rental increase measure on 3 June 2026](https://adrec.gov.ae/en/news/press-release-26---rental-freeze-update), describing a 0% annual increase for the duration of the measure and reference to the last registered Tawtheeq contract. Verify whether it remains in force and how it applies to your proposed lease; do not assume an arbitrary annual increase or that the temporary measure lasts for the entire example.

Review the written lease, deposit, maintenance, notice and early-exit provisions. ADREC's [document verification service](https://adrec.gov.ae/en/verify-document) includes tenancy contracts. Confirm the current registration process and charges with the relevant parties.

Record the apartment's condition and included items at handover, and keep the lease and receipts.

sections.heading: Check purchase costs and the building
sections.body:
DARI's [sale registration service](https://services.dari.ae/consumer-services/registration-of-sale-and-purchase-of-land-and-real-estate/) lists the process and charges for its stated service. The [Abu Dhabi buying cost guide](/journal/total-cost-of-buying-an-apartment-in-abu-dhabi) explains how fee allocation and other costs affect the buyer's budget. Obtain an itemised current quote.

Confirm the buyer's ownership right, title, seller authority, any mortgage or tenancy and required clearance. Inspect the apartment and shared facilities and request the current service-charge statement. A waterfront view or building amenity must be checked for the actual unit.

Keep a reserve for repairs and consider how long a future sale might take.

sections.heading: Match the choice to your plans
sections.body:
A short or uncertain stay makes transaction and moving costs more significant. A longer stay spreads one-off costs over more years; include a range of sale prices in the comparison. Renting can also involve renewal uncertainty and moving costs.

Test a range of sale prices, length of stay and financing assumptions. Consider a change in work or family needs and whether the lease or sale process provides the flexibility required. Choose a plan that remains affordable under more than one plausible outcome.

Inspect the actual building, parking and daily routes for each option. Check the current service-charge statement for a purchase and what utilities or cooling a tenant must pay. A comparable apartment is useful only if it meets the same household requirements and its terms are verified.

sections.heading: Request current Al Reem options
sections.body:
Browse [Aliyas Al Reem Island projects](/projects?emirate=Abu%20Dhabi&area=abu-dhabi-al-reem-island) and [contact Aliyas](/contact) with your budget and intended stay. Ask which purchase or rental homes are currently available and request their exact terms and the relevant unit documents.

Use written quotes and your own cash-flow assumptions before making a decision about the home.
